- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.00 or +0.67 in consecutive days), especially in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.33) or shows recent downward momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts; model should not overshoot 2–3 days after sentiment turns positive.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, model should not ignore it — adjust forecast downward if sentiment turns negative within 2 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; reduce by 0.5–1.5% per day for those days.
- Don’t ignore sentiment history when correcting — if sentiment was consistently positive for 3+ days, model should not forecast a sharp drop unless sentiment turns negative.
